name: Battle of San Jacinto
note: The accounts do not give compass directions or the exact positions of the Mexican troops, who are shown as one body behind their breastworks. The Mexican camp lay on a plain with woods on one side and marsh and lake on another; the plan puts the woods at the left and the marsh and lake at the top, and does not claim these were their true bearings. Vince's Bridge lay about 8 miles from the Texian camp, so only the direction Santa Anna took is drawn. The Texian riflemen on the lake banks are shown as a small part of the Texian infantry; the accounts do not say which regiment supplied them.

terrain.quote: The Texians made camp in a wooded area along the bank of Buffalo Bayou

terrain.name: Woods
terrain.quote: bordered by woods on one side, marsh and lake on another

terrain.name: Marsh
terrain.quote: Many Mexican soldiers retreated through the marsh to Peggy Lake.

units.name: Texian second regiment
units.quote: The second regiment, under the command of Colonel Sydney Sherman (sic), formed the left-wing of the army.

units.name: Texian centre

units.quote: four companies under the command of Lieutenant Colonel Henry Millard, sustained the artillery on the right

units.name: Texian cavalry

units.name: Mexican army
units.quote: Throughout the night, Mexican troops worked to fortify their camp

units.name: Santa Anna and staff
units.quote: Santa Anna, Castrillón, and Almonte yelled often conflicting orders

phases.title: The armies face each other across the grass
phases.text: Houston drew up the Texian line with the second regiment on the left, Burleson in the centre, the artillery and Millard's companies on the right and the cavalry on the extreme right. The Mexican troops lay behind breastworks in their camp.
phases.quote: The two camps were approximately 500 yards (460 m) apart, separated by a grassy area with a slight rise in the middle.

phases.title: The cavalry go wide and the guns move up
phases.text: The Texian cavalry was sent to the Mexican far left, and the artillery advanced through the tall grass to within 200 yards of the breastworks.
phases.quote: The Texian cavalry was first dispatched to the Mexican forces' far left, and the artillery advanced through the tall grass to within 200 yards of the Mexican breastworks.

phases.title: The Twin Sisters fire and the Texians rush the camp
phases.text: The Twin Sisters fired and began the battle. After a single volley the Texians broke ranks and swarmed over the breastworks, and the surprised Mexican officers shouted conflicting orders.
phases.quote: After a single volley, Texians broke ranks and swarmed over the Mexican breastworks

phases.title: The breastworks fall and the Mexican troops flee
phases.text: The Texian infantry advanced until they held the woodland and the breastworks. Within 18 minutes the Mexican soldiers left their camp and fled. Santa Anna escaped towards Vince's Bridge.
phases.quote: Within 18 minutes, Mexican soldiers abandoned their campsite and fled for their lives.

phases.title: Pursuit to Peggy Lake
phases.text: Many Mexican soldiers retreated through the marsh to Peggy Lake, where Texian riflemen stationed themselves on the banks and shot at anything that moved. The killing lasted for hours.
phases.quote: Texian riflemen stationed themselves on the banks and shot at anything that moved.
